review_notes: Read the whole file, focusing on the WCOT* namespaces and the two long COTGlue theorems. Three repetitions stood out: a verbatim copied 25-line lemma, a ~25-line basis-straightening block shared by the two main theorems, and the 'T lies on the line' derivation. I did not compile any replacement. In the proposed shared lemmas, placement and name qualification (namespaces, p2m_export of the private sl2M copies) are the likely friction points. The three separate private sl2M definitions are probably forced by the p2m_export mechanism, so I did not report them separately.

findings.excerpt: theorem trace_eq_zero_of_mul_self_eq_zero (N : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) R) (hN : N * N = 0) : N.trace = 0 := by
findings.problem: The same 24-line proof appears twice, once in WCOTDevB6 (402–425) and once in WCOTGlueBAdapt (458–482). It extracts the four entry equations of N*N=0 and then runs the same case analysis (the trace is nonzero, so b=c=0, so a²=d²=0). The two copies differ only in how the NoZeroDivisors hypothesis is stated. A fix to one copy would not reach the other.
findings.proposed_change: State the lemma once, as `theorem WCOTGlueBCore.trace_eq_zero_of_mul_self_eq_zero {R} [CommRing R] [NoZeroDivisors R] (N : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) R) (hN : N * N = 0) : N.trace = 0`, with the existing proof, in the WCOTGlueBCore block (around line 359). The `{R : Type} [CommRing R]` variable there lacks NoZeroDivisors, so add it to the lemma binder. Delete the two copies. In `WCOTDevB6.eq_line_of_unipotent_mul` (line 429) and in `WCOTGlueBAdapt.exists_conj_eq_sl2M` (about line 489), call `WCOTGlueBCore.trace_eq_zero_of_mul_self_eq_zero N hN` or `M hM`. The hypotheses are unchanged: both users already have NoZeroDivisors R (B6 through its variable, Adapt through IsDomain R). The proof only needs Matrix.mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_two, mul_eq_zero and mul_self_eq_zero, which are available through the existing imports.
findings.benefit: This removes about 25 duplicated lines and leaves one proof to maintain and read. The ring-theoretic content (N²=0 forces trace 0 over a reduced ring) then has one canonical home instead of two identical copies in different namespaces.

findings.excerpt: obtain ⟨Pm, hPm, t, ht, hconj⟩ := WCOTGlueBAdapt.exists_conj_eq_sl2M _ hN₀sq hN₀ne
findings.problem: Both main theorems open with the same ~25-line setup. First comes `hchar`, which turns hunip into a charpoly statement for `endToMatrix ρ b (ρ.ρ τ)` in any basis b. Then they pick `b₀ := finBasisOfFinrankEq`, show N₀ = T₀ − 1 squares to zero and is nonzero, and apply `exists_conj_eq_sl2M`. Finally they rebuild the basis `b₀.map (Matrix.toLinearEquiv b₀ Pm hPm)` and prove `hT₀b : endToMatrix ρ b (ρ.ρ τ₀) = 1 + sl2M 0 t 0`. This is lines 629–654 in phaseB and 795–816 in frob_tame_rel, and the text is essentially identical. It is the substantive step 'choose a basis in which a nontrivial unipotent inertia element is 1 + t·E'. It is pasted into two proofs that are otherwise unrelated.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma in `namespace COTGlue`, after WCOTGlueBFinal and before phaseB, so that WCOTGlueBAdapt, WCOTGlueBT1 and sl2M are all in scope. Statement: for `ρ : GaloisRepAdic 𝒪` with 𝒪 a DVR, a prime-lying-over hypothesis in the form `hI : ∀ τ ∈ P.inertiaSubgroupIn ℚ, LinearMap.charpoly (ρ.ρ τ) = (X-1)^2`, and `τ₀ ∈ P.inertiaSubgroupIn ℚ` with `ρ.ρ τ₀ ≠ 1`, conclude `∃ (b : Basis (Fin 2) 𝒪 ρ.V) (t : 𝒪), t ≠ 0 ∧ endToMatrix ρ b (ρ.ρ τ₀) = 1 + sl2M 0 t 0`. The proof is the existing lines 635–654 verbatim. Pair it with a small lemma `endToMatrix_charpoly_eq` (for all b and τ ∈ I, `(endToMatrix ρ b (ρ.ρ τ)).charpoly = (X-1)^2`), which replaces the two `hchar` blocks. phaseB then starts `obtain ⟨b, t, ht, hT₀b⟩ := exists_basis_one_add_sl2M ρ (hunip P hP) τ₀ hτ₀P hτ₀ne`. frob_tame_rel does the same, using `hunip P hP` and its `hτ₀P`, `hτ₀ne`. Both proofs keep their own downstream hypotheses (`hsq`, `htr`, `hline'`, `hf`), which depend on the chosen basis.
findings.benefit: The two long proofs shrink by about 25 lines each. The basis-straightening argument is stated once with a meaningful name and statement, so a reader sees what it provides without comparing two copies. Any later fix, such as changing the base-change convention, happens in one place.

findings.excerpt: have key := WCOTDevB6.eq_line_of_unipotent_mul t ht (T - 1) hN hu
findings.problem: The step 'a matrix T with (T−1)²=0 and trace((1+tE)·T)=2 lies on the line, T = 1 + b·E' is proved twice by the same script. Each copy sets `hT1 : 1 + (T - 1) = T`, rewrites the trace statement into `WCOTDevB6.sl2M` form, applies `eq_line_of_unipotent_mul`, and rewrites back with `sl2M_B6_eq`. This is `hline` in matrix_length_le (589–597) and `hline'` in frob_tame_rel (818–828). Only the final coefficient form differs (`sl2M 0 b 0` versus `a • sl2M 0 1 0`).
findings.proposed_change: In WCOTGlueBFinal, after `sl2M_B6_eq`, add `theorem eq_one_add_sl2M_of_trace {R} [CommRing R] [NoZeroDivisors R] (t : R) (ht : t ≠ 0) (T : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) R) (hsq : (T-1)*(T-1) = 0) (htr : ((1 + sl2M 0 t 0) * T).trace = 2) : T = 1 + sl2M 0 (T-1 : Matrix _ _ R) 0 1 0`. Here WCOTGlueBFinal opens WCOTGlueBCore, so sl2M is the Core copy, and the proof is lines 590–597 verbatim. The IsDomain R hypothesis of matrix_length_le provides NoZeroDivisors. Then `hline := fun T hT => ⟨_, eq_one_add_sl2M_of_trace t ht T (hsq T hT) (htr T hT)⟩`. In frob_tame_rel, `hline'` becomes `⟨_, (eq_one_add_sl2M_of_trace t ht T hN hu').trans (by rw [sl2M_smul_eq])⟩`, where `hu'` is the existing `trace_eq_two_of_charpoly` computation without the `sl2M_B6_eq` rewriting.
findings.benefit: This removes the duplicated T−1 / sl2M_B6_eq conversion boilerplate in two places. The conversions between the three definitionally equal copies of sl2M are then confined to a single lemma instead of leaking into each caller.
